A 27-year-old woman was introduced to the department with elevated hepatobiliary enzymes. The patient occasionally drank alcohol. She had no history of viral hepatitis, steatohepatitis, autoimmune liver disease, or metabolic liver disease. The patient was taking axitinib, azelnidipine, and tramadol hydrochloride. After stopping alcohol and axitinib, her hepatobiliary enzyme levels remained unchanged.
No specific physical examination findings were reported in the case.
